pairings.title: Calm creative workspace
pairings.why: Glass supports a small number of floating controls; opaque bento cards organise working information. Tabs make the relationship between a choice and its content clear.
pairings.recipe: Warm white, sage-grey and charcoal. Reserve glass for navigation or inspectors. Keep project cards opaque and animate only the selected content.
pairings.avoid: Blur on every card, competing hover effects and a moving background beneath long text.

pairings.title: Family recipe library
pairings.why: Natural materials and hand-drawn ingredients give the collection warmth. A shared-element transition keeps the selected book or recipe recognisable.
pairings.recipe: Linen, cream and deep green. Illustrated book covers, readable recipe type and one gentle transition into the detail view.
pairings.avoid: Multiple incompatible drawing styles, noisy textures under instructions and a page flip required for every task.

pairings.title: Agency production dashboard
pairings.why: Editorial restraint gives the work room; a modular grid summarises status. A stable relationship map explains dependencies and reordering supports the actual plan.
pairings.recipe: Off-white, dark olive and one lilac accent. Prioritise approvals, next actions and active work. Make rearrangement explicit and reversible.
pairings.avoid: Decorative live-looking metrics, excessive node motion and equal visual weight for every card.

pairings.title: Outdoor event storytelling
pairings.why: Botanical detail, physical paper layers and contours share a landscape language. Restrained parallax reinforces foreground and background.
pairings.recipe: Forest, parchment and warm clay. Use one bounded story scene, then practical sections for materials, activities and setup.
pairings.avoid: Full-page scroll effects, animals covering text and a long animated journey before the checklist.

pairings.title: Technical mechanism explainer
pairings.why: Technical typography and isometric structure support a clear layered explanation. A real product sequence gives the diagram a task and purpose.
pairings.recipe: Cool ivory, charcoal and muted blue. Start assembled, separate along one axis, then hold numbered component explanations.
pairings.avoid: Unverified dimensions, dramatic camera spins and dozens of simultaneous unlabeled parts.

pairings.title: Cinematic product launch
pairings.why: Quiet editorial type balances a reflective signature object. A short scrub sequence can explain one transformation without filling the whole page with motion.
pairings.recipe: Dark ink, pale silver and a soft accent. Introduce the product immediately, use one sculptural sequence, then show readable features.
pairings.avoid: Endless reveal scrolling, tiny copy and reflections that hide the subject.

clashes.title: Glass + fine grain + moving texture
clashes.body: All three compete at the surface level. Keep the glass lightly tinted, put grain in a static background and leave reading cards opaque.

clashes.title: Neon + glitch + moire
clashes.body: High contrast, temporal disruption and interference create competing focal points. Use one as the signature effect and keep the other two static or absent.

clashes.title: Springs + tilt + magnetic targets
clashes.body: Several physical responses can make a control feel unstable. Keep the hit target fixed and choose a single small movement for the action.

clashes.title: Paper collage + liquid metal
clashes.body: These materials can coexist in a campaign, but need a clear hierarchy. Let one own the main scene and use the other in a separate supporting moment.

clashes.title: Bento + equal-size priorities
clashes.body: A varied grid loses its purpose if every card demands attention. Establish the main task first, then subordinate supporting modules.

clashes.title: Technical diagrams + decorative data
clashes.body: Precision implies evidence. Label conceptual diagrams and separate atmosphere from actual quantities, measurements and engineering claims.

references.title: Meet Liquid Glass
references.creator: Apple · WWDC25
references.note: Study how the material supports controls, navigation and hierarchy in Apple's own presentation.

references.title: Tonhalle Zurich concert poster
references.creator: Josef Muller-Brockmann · MoMA collection
references.note: Look at scale, alignment and typographic structure in the museum's record of the poster.

references.title: Fourier series and circle drawings
references.creator: Grant Sanderson · 3Blue1Brown
references.note: Compare a computed construction with a decorative circle drawing; follow the rotating-vector explanation.

references.title: Hand-Crafted Cinema
references.creator: Caroline Leaf · National Film Board of Canada
references.note: A workshop covering sand, paint-on-glass and scratch animation, with examples from Leaf's work.

references.title: Pinscreen
references.creator: Alexandre Alexeieff and Claire Parker · NFB
references.note: See the actual physical pinboard mechanism and the relationship between relief and shadows.

references.title: Mindscape
references.creator: Jacques Drouin · National Film Board of Canada
references.note: View a finished pinscreen film alongside the physical-technique demonstration.

references.title: Paper Cut-outs
references.creator: National Film Board of Canada
references.note: Explore the cut-out tradition through the publisher's account of NFB and Norman McLaren work.

references.title: Wallace & Gromit
references.creator: Nick Park · Aardman
references.note: Study tangible character materials, expressive poses and stop-motion staging in original studio work.

references.title: Into the Spider-Verse
references.creator: Sony Pictures Animation
references.note: Use the studio reference to study a distinctive graphic and dimensional visual language, rather than treating a style name as a complete brief.

references.title: Rendering Worlds with Two Triangles
references.creator: Inigo Quilez
references.note: An original presentation about compact graphics and raymarching; useful for separating technique from appearance.

references.title: The Algorithmic Beauty of Plants
references.creator: Przemyslaw Prusinkiewicz and Aristid Lindenmayer · Algorithmic Botany
references.note: Study formal growth rules and branching models at the authors' research archive.

references.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting
references.creator: Bernhard Kerbl, Georgios Kopanas, Thomas Leimkuehler and George Drettakis
references.note: Inspect the authors' project and examples; Gaussian splatting is a specific representation, not a synonym for glowing points.

references.title: Voronoi maps tutorial
references.creator: Amit Patel · Red Blob Games
references.note: Use the interactive map tutorial to see a constructed polygon partition and its implementation.

references.title: Pillars of Creation
references.creator: NASA · ESA · CSA · Webb
references.note: Inspect real astronomical imagery and its explanation. Generated cosmic artwork should remain separately labelled.

references.title: Spline Academy
references.creator: Spline
references.note: The publisher's tutorials include interactive spatial scenes, voxel characters, toon shading and shape-blending demonstrations.

references.title: Carousel animations
references.creator: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative
references.note: Read the original guidance for controlling rotation and handling focus and hover.
